page.layout: Running head at top; two round portrait medallions with legends side by side (left: Tiberius Gracchus, right: Cornelia); one column of running text below, two paragraphs; signature mark at lower right of the text block. No margin notes.

main_text.l: TRIBVNVS TIB. GRACCHVS
CORNELIA GRA MATER CH.[?]
TIB. GRACCHVS Tribunus plebis, certauit de lege
agraria pro egenis aduersus diuites,quo tēpore Africanus Sci-
pio apud Numantiam pugnabat. Nam Romani quantum vi-
cini agri hostibus adimebant,partim venundare,partim in pu-
blicum redigere, ac egenis ciuibus pro modica pensione vten-
dum tradere cōsueuerant:sed diuitibus pensiones augentibus,
pauperēsque excludentibus , lata est lex,quæ supra quingenta
agri iugera ciuem Romanū possidere vetabat. Hæc lex paucos
annos aduersus locupletes auxilio fuit. Nam primò conductis
personis fraus legi fiebat : deinde apertè iam per seipsos occu-
pare agros diuites cœperant. Pauperum itaque partes fouens
Gracchus,diuitum inuidia contraxit:in ipsoque tumultu dum
fugere tentat , toga retentus , pede subsellij caput percutitur à
P.Saturnino,vno ex principibus,&,cum aliis triginta, fustibus
& lapidibus mactatur:quorum corpora fuerunt proiecta in Ty-
berim,anno mundi 3831.ante Christum natum 131. Plut.in vita
Grac.Appi.li.1.Eutr.li.4.
CORNELIA Africani filia,Tiberij & Caij Gracchorum
mater, marito vidua hos sic educauit,vt cum magnitudine in-
dolis cæteros omnes anteirent, doctrina tamen quàm natura
prævaluisse viderentur.hæc relicta cum duodecim filiis,Ptole-
maei regis nuptias respuit : cum ille regni & diadematis com-
municationem offerret. Deinde decem ex filiis obierunt, su-
pradictis duobus relictis : filiam Africano minori collocauit.
Plutar.in Tibe.& Ca.Gracchis.

page.notes: Two round woodcut medallions at top with legends printed around the rim; the legend letters are small and partly worn, so the right-hand medallion legend is doubtful, especially the abbreviation after GRA and the final "CH." The first paragraph has "pensione" with a long-s-like form; read as printed. Some letters in the Greek-free text are faint, notably "ante Christum", "Plut.in" and the abbreviations in the footnote-style references at the end of paragraphs. No catchword is visible.
